subject: AWS private-offer: SKU mapping and billing split discussion
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Cheng <emily@resellco.com>, David Nguyen <david.nguyen@amazon.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: AWS private-offer: SKU mapping and billing split discussion

Hi Emily / David —

Thanks again for the quick sync last week. To keep momentum on the AWS Channel Private Offer (ResellCo -> Redwood) we need to lock two operational pieces before we start activation:

1) SKU mapping: confirm which reseller SKUs will map to our hosted SKUs so AWS can reconcile usage to the private offer line item.
2) Billing split & invoice flow: confirm whether ResellCo will invoice the end customer directly and then settle with Redwood, or whether AWS should route settlement via their marketplace flow.

I attached a first-draft SKU mapping spreadsheet (ResellCo_SKU_Mapping_V1.xlsx) and a short draft reseller SOW to illustrate the proposed invoice milestones. Can you please:
- Confirm the mapping columns that your finance team needs (account-level vs. subscriber-level SKUs).
- Confirm how you want tax/VAT handled for US customers (ResellCo invoice vs. AWS-managed tax).

Once we have agreement on those two items, we can open the CPPO in AWS with the correct line-item configuration and initiate the DocuSign SOW.

Suggested next steps: Emily — if your finance ops lead can review the attached mapping by EOD Wednesday (6/16) we’ll schedule a short 30-min call with David to align on AWS settlement mechanics.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Channel Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: ResellCo_SKU_Mapping_V1.xlsx, Draft-Reseller-SOW-ResellCo.pdf

From: Emily Cheng <emily@resellco.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, David Nguyen <david.nguyen@amazon.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: AWS private-offer: SKU mapping and billing split discussion

Thanks Vanessa —

Quick responses from ResellCo side after a fast review:
- SKU mapping: your sheet format looks good. Finance prefers account-level SKUs tied to the AWS subscriber ID rather than a global SKU per product. That makes reconciliation easier on our side.
- Billing / tax: for US customers we usually invoice directly (ResellCo -> Customer) and handle tax on our invoices. We can do AWS-managed tax if Redwood prefers that flow, but our legal team will want to confirm exposure.

Two requests: can you add a "customer-subscriber-id" column to the mapping so our auto-recon tool can ingest it? Also please send the SOW to our legal review queue (legal@resellco.com) once it's final.

Happy to jump on a call Wed afternoon if that works.

Best,
Emily Cheng
Head of Partnerships, ResellCo
emily@resellco.com

Team — looping you in. ResellCo prefers account-level SKUs and will invoice end customers (they can take tax exposure). They asked for a customer-subscriber-id column in our mapping.

Questions for finance / billing ops:
- Is account-level SKU mapping OK for our AWS CPPO configuration, or does it complicate AWS procurement flow?
- If ResellCo invoices directly, what does that mean for Redwood revenue recognition and our revenue reporting in HubSpot / billing?

I attached the draft mapping. Ben — can you take the lead on a proposed billing diagram we can send to ResellCo and David? Marcus — can you confirm whether the customer-subscriber-id field can be populated from our tenant metadata export?

I want to get back to Emily with a proposed flow + diagram by EOD today so we can run legal on the SOW tomorrow.

Thanks —
Vanessa

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: AWS private-offer: SKU mapping and billing split discussion

Vanessa —

Quick notes from finance ops after a sync with Marcus:
- Account-level SKU mapping is fine. For the CPPO we will create a single private-offer line item that references the mapping table. AWS supports a per-subscriber reconciliation column (we've used the AWS "customerIdentifier" field before).
- If ResellCo invoices the end customer, Redwood will recognize gross revenue and then record a cost-of-revenue transfer to ResellCo per the SOW. We'll need the reseller's W-9 and bank details pre-DocuSign.
- Tax: if ResellCo handles tax on their invoices, Redwood needs a statement in the SOW that shifts tax liability to them for US customers; otherwise we'll default to AWS-managed tax.

Action items I can own:
1) Draft a one-page billing diagram and flow (will attach).
2) Update the mapping sheet to include "customer-subscriber-id" and a "reconciliation_key" column.
3) Create a secure upload link for ResellCo to send W-9 + bank details.

I'll attach the billing diagram and a DocuSign pre-fill link for the SOW in the next email.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Finance Operations
ben.carter@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: AWS private-offer: SKU mapping and billing split discussion — proposed plan and next steps

Hi Emily / David —

Following internal alignment, here is the proposed operational plan (summary):

1) SKU mapping: we will send an updated mapping CSV (attached) with a customer-subscriber-id column and reconciliation_key. ResellCo to validate by EOD Wed (6/16).
2) Billing & tax: ResellCo will invoice end customers and handle US tax. We will add a clause in the SOW assigning US tax liability to ResellCo.
3) AWS CPPO: once SKU mapping is finalized we will request CPPO creation with AWS referencing the reconciliation_key for per-subscriber usage. David — please confirm AWS is OK with the reconciliation_key approach (we've used it on other deals).
4) Docs & evidence: ResellCo to upload W-9 + bank details to the secure link Ben will provide. We will then route the final SOW via DocuSign (link below).
